correctness.rationale: The disk geodesic is a circle orthogonal to the boundary. The hyperboloid signed-distance formula gives each of the n−1 midpoint distances exactly, with adjacent sides nearest. On the complete side, the two adjacent distances grow/decay exponentially in arc-length coordinate, so their minimum is strictly maximized at the midpoint. The asymptotic follows from Taylor expansion; the numerical checker corroborates but does not prove the unrestricted formula.

value.rationale: Polygonal side slimness is the actual natural invariant emphasized in current metric-geometry papers. The exact all-n regular-ideal benchmark and unique extremal side points establish a bounded, monotone saturation law despite increasing side count; this separates a symmetric polygon subfamily from the potentially growing global slimness function and supplies a normalization benchmark for testing sharpness claims. It is not merely a finite test or isolated substitution.
